newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close mixed, 2nd board continues fall.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close mixed, 2nd board continues fall.

text.p: Malaysian equities closed mixed, with blue-chip stocks posting moderate gains, and small-cap issues falling.

"Local (institutions) have been buying Tenaga, Telekom and Petronas Gas, while the foreigners have been buying United Engineers, Tan Chong and gaming stocks," said an institutional dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.

The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks was up 1.68 points to 1,196.08, while the Second Board index was down 6.16 to 641.27. Tenaga, a major contributor to the weightage of the composite Index, was up 20 cents to 11.30 ringgit.
Telekom closed up 10 cents to 23.20 ringgit, Petronas Gas was unchanged at 10.20, Magnum gained eight to 4.54, and Tan Chong rose 22 to 4.46.
"All the bad news on Tenaga and Telekom has been discounted now," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas.
Petronas Gas was actively traded on positive statements about the future of natural gas by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Monday, Tan said.
Gaming firm Magnum was up on better-than-expected half-year results of competitor Berjaya Sports Toto on Monday, he said.
